prest.definition:
imp. & p. p. of Press.
a. Ready; prompt; prepared.
a. Neat; tidy; proper.
n. Ready money; a loan of money.
n. A duty in money formerly paid by the sheriff on his account
   in the exchequer, or for money left or remaining in his hands.
v. t. To give as a loan; to lend.
prest.translation: n. 普雷斯特（英钟表工匠, 1820年取得表的无钥匙机能的专利）

prestain.translation: 预先染色, 预先着色

prestation.definition:
n. A payment of money; a toll or duty; also, the rendering
   of a service.
prestation.translation: [法] 给付, 履行, 付款

prestel.translation: n. （英国邮电系统的）快速电视电话咨询服务

prester.definition:
n. A meteor or exhalation formerly supposed to be thrown from
   the clouds with such violence that by collision it is set on fire.
n. One of the veins of the neck when swollen with anger or
   other excitement.
n. A priest or presbyter; as, Prester John.

presternal notch.translation: [医] 胸骨前切迹, 锁骨间切迹

presternum.definition: n. The anterior segment of the sternum; the manubrium.

prestidigitation.definition: n. manual dexterity in the execution of tricks

prestidigitator.definition: n someone who performs magic tricks to amuse an audience

prestige.definition: n. a high standing achieved through success or influence or wealth etc.
prestige.translation:
n. 声望, 威望, 威信
[经] 商誉, 声誉

prestigeful.translation:
有威信的
有影响力的

prestigious.definition: s. exerting influence by reason of high status or prestige

prestigiousness.definition: n. a high standing achieved through success or influence or wealth etc.

prestissimo.definition:
s (of tempo) as fast as possible
r extremely fast; as fast as possible
prestissimo.translation:
n. 最快速度
a. 最快的, 极快的

presto.definition:
s. (of tempo) very fast
r. suddenly
r. at a very fast tempo (faster than allegro)
presto.translation:
adv. 赶快, 转眼间, 立刻
a. 变戏法似的

prestomal.translation: .唇瓣裂的, 与唇瓣裂有关的

preston.translation: n. 普勒斯顿（男子名；英国港市名字）

prestone.translation: [化] 普列斯通(一种低凝固点液体乙二醇系防冻剂)

prestonsburg.translation: [地名] [英国、英国] 普雷斯顿斯堡

prestress.translation:
vt. 对...预加应力
[化] 预应力; 预加应力

prestwood.translation: [地名] [英国] 普雷斯特伍德
